newsitem.title: UK: Russia higher in quiet emerging debt market.
newsitem.headline: Russia higher in quiet emerging debt market.

text.p: Russia, buoyed by positive signals over the weekend for the future of its economy, led emerging market debt higher on Monday but trading overall was light.
Traders said it was getting increasingly hard to drum up business as the end of the year approached and in a market still uncertain about the influence from U.S. markets.

On Friday, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) agreed to release the delayed October tranche of its RUssia loan programme. On Sunday, the government managed to get its draft 1997 budget proposals through their first reading in the State Duma.
After two more readings, the budget has to go to the upper house for approval.
The market is now waiting to see when the IMF will rElease the November and December tranches of the loan, but traders said the latest news adds to the positive view of Russia.
Vneshekonombank debt and the when-and-if paper it will become when Russia's commercial debt rescheduling deal is closed, possibly by next March,all rose by up to 3/4 of a point.
One trader said there was a fair amount of activity in Russia debt options as investors adjusted delta positions.
MinFins were also slightly higher with some local buying in Russia, traders said.
They said the general trend of the emerging debt market has taken a turn for the better after rising on Friday on the back of firmer U.S. Treasuries.
"Overall the market is looking good. Global markets are calmer and there's some positive news around," one said.
But he added that there was little chance of any major movements until January.
